page: Microsoft Azure E16as_v4 is an EASv4-series virtual machine configured with 16 vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The underlying hardware features an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. This setup delivers 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, utilizing dedicated CPU allocation. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instructions.

The instance includes 262 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, scoring 2698.78 in stress-ng single-core tests, and a strong PassMark memory score of 2788.92. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth tests fall within the average tier, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 80.83 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 45.68 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also perform at average levels, yielding 7056.09 operations and 16.14 million operations per second respectively.

While the server handles smaller language models adequately, it exhibits weaker performance on larger workloads, such as LLM inference with a medium 7B model, which processes prompts at 30.4 tokens per second. Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU and solid memory performance, this instance is structured for memory-intensive workloads. It is appropriate for relational databases, in-memory caching layers, data buffering, and enterprise applications requiring a balance of dedicated AMD EPYC processing and substantial memory capacity without dedicated GPU acceleration.
